name: The Meridian Line
facts: The Meridian Line is a railway that was built in 1954 by the engineer Halvard Steen.
Halvard Steen was born in the town of Brevik and trained as a bridge engineer.
The Meridian Line runs between Brevik and the port city of Alstad.
The port at Alstad handles timber, which is the main cargo carried on the Meridian Line.
The Meridian Line has 14 stations, of which 3 are underground.
The three underground stations on the Meridian Line are Alstad Central, Fjordgate and Nyhavn.
Fjordgate station was closed in 1998 after flooding damaged its lower platform.
The flood of 1998 was caused by the failure of the Brevik sea wall.
The Brevik sea wall was designed by Halvard Steen in 1961.
After the 1998 flood, timber traffic on the Meridian Line was rerouted through Nyhavn.
Nyhavn station was expanded in 2001 to handle the extra freight.
The Meridian Line uses a narrow gauge of 1067 millimetres.
